title: Your £20,000 ISA Limit Is Quietly Shrinking… Then Cash Savers Get Just £12,000 😱🛡️ #shorts
description:
Your ISA limit is £20,000, but it's quietly shrinking.

When ISAs began in April 1999 the limit was £7,000 a year (HMRC). Prices (ONS CPI) have almost doubled since: up 99.6% from April 1999 to September 2026, so keeping pace would have needed about £14,000 (£13,971). The limit is £20,000, so it beat prices since 1999.

The catch: it has been £20,000 since 6 April 2017, frozen for over nine years. Prices have risen just over 40% since April 2017, so keeping pace would now take about £28,000 (£28,008). Put the other way, today's £20,000 buys what about £14,300 did in April 2017.

Then from 6 April 2027, the cash ISA limit drops to £12,000 a year if you're under 65 (£20,000 if you're 65 or over). The overall ISA limit stays £20,000 (gov.uk says until April 2031), so the other £8,000 can only go into other types of ISA, such as stocks and shares.

Sources: HMRC ISA statistics, Table 9.4 (limits 1999-2018): https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/737084/Table_9.4_Published_August_2018.pdf · HMRC Annual savings statistics 2026, background (limits to 2026-27): https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/annual-savings-statistics-2026/annual-savings-statistics-background-and-methodology · HMRC Tax-free savings newsletter 19 (cash ISA from April 2027): https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/tax-free-savings-newsletter-19/tax-free-savings-newsletter-19-november-2025 · ONS CPI index D7BT: https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/timeseries/d7bt
